# curequantile

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The curequantile package can be used to fit quantile regression model for 
censored time-to-event data with a cure fraction.

## Installation

You can install the development version of curequantile by issuing:

``` r
remotes::install_github("kelliejarcher/curequantile")
```

## Example

After loading the relevant R packages,

```{r libraries}
library(curequantile)
library(survival)
library(maxLik)
```

a cure quantile regression model can be fit using the `curequantile` function.

```{r example}
data("breast_data")
fit_breast <- curequantile(Surv(log(Time), Delta) ~ Age + Size,
  data = breast_data, subset = 1:200)
```

The `coef()` function extracts the parameter estimates at a specific quantile 
`tau`.

```{r coef}
coefficients <- coef(fit_breast, tau = 0.25)
names(coefficients)
coefficients$gamma_est
```

Here, `gamma_est` contains the incidence parameter estimates, while `beta_est` 
contains the latency parameter estimates at the specified quantile, `tau`. 
Finally, `eta_est` gives the conditional probabilities of being susceptible, and 
therefore has a length equal to the number of rows in the input data frame. 
Alternatively, `print()` prints the coefficients at the user-specified quantile
`tau` to the console.

The `summary()` function returns the parameter estimates, bootstrap standard 
error estimates, Z-test, p-value, and bootstrap confidence interval for 
incidence covariates and the latency covariates at the indicated quantile, 
`tau`.

The `plot()` function produces a plot of the quantile estimate and corresponding 
confidence interval for each covariate over the range of the user-specified 
quantiles `tau`.

Other functions designed to handle the resulting model object include: `dim()`, 
`formula()`, `logLik()`, `nobs()`, and `predict()`.
